name: Custom (generic risk & control)
description: A domain-neutral risk and control checklist built on the COSO and ISO 31000 risk lifecycle, covering governance, risk assessment, access, data, change, third parties, monitoring, incidents and continuity. Use it as a starting point for any risk area and tailor the wording.
references: COSO Internal Control - Integrated Framework (2013), COSO ERM (2017), ISO 31000:2018, IIA Three Lines Model

categories.name: Governance & Oversight
categories.objective: The risk area has clear ownership, appetite, obligations and senior oversight.

items.control: An executive sponsor and a risk owner are named and accountable for the risk area.
items.risk: Risks go unmanaged because no one owns them.
items.test: Inspect the RACI or appointment record and confirm the named individuals are current.
evidence: Risk owner field in the GRC tool

items.control: Risk appetite and tolerances for the area are defined in measurable terms and approved by senior management.
items.risk: Decisions take on more risk than leadership would accept.
items.test: Inspect the appetite statement for measurable tolerances and approval within 12 months.

items.control: A governance forum meets on a defined cadence, records decisions and escalates issues beyond tolerance.
items.risk: Issues are not escalated to people with authority to act.
items.test: Inspect terms of reference and minutes for each meeting in the period, and trace escalated issues to decisions.

items.control: Roles, responsibilities and competence requirements are documented, and role-holders are trained.
items.risk: People perform controls they do not understand.
items.test: For sampled control owners, confirm documented responsibilities and completed role training.

items.control: Staff acknowledge the code of conduct annually, and breaches are investigated.
items.risk: Unethical behaviour undermines controls.
items.test: Compare acknowledgement records to the HR roster and inspect the conduct case log.
evidence: Acknowledgement report compared to the HR roster

items.control: Applicable legal, regulatory and contractual obligations are inventoried with owners and mapped to controls.
items.risk: Obligations are missed, leading to fines or breach of contract.
items.test: Inspect the obligations register for owners and control mapping, and confirm it was updated for new requirements in the period.

items.control: Management reviews the effectiveness of the risk programme annually and records improvement actions.
items.risk: The programme stagnates while risks evolve.
items.test: Inspect management review minutes and confirm actions were tracked.

categories.name: Risk Assessment
categories.objective: Risks are identified, rated consistently and given treatment.

items.control: A documented method defines likelihood and impact scales and rating criteria for risk assessment.
items.risk: Ratings are subjective and inconsistent, so priorities are wrong.
items.test: Inspect the method and re-perform the rating for a sample of risks.

items.control: A risk register records inherent and residual ratings, owners and linked controls, and is reviewed quarterly.
items.risk: Known risks are lost or left stale.
items.test: For a sample of risks, confirm complete fields and a review in each quarter.
evidence: Risk register export from the GRC tool

items.control: Risk assessments are refreshed annually and when there is significant change (new product, system, process, regulation or acquisition).
items.risk: New risks from change go unassessed.
items.test: Compare significant changes in the period to assessments performed.
evidence: List of significant changes in the period

items.control: Fraud risk (misappropriation, misreporting, corruption) is explicitly assessed.
items.risk: Fraud schemes exploit gaps nobody considered.
items.test: Inspect the fraud risk assessment for scenarios and linked anti-fraud controls.

items.control: Risk treatment plans have owners and due dates and are tracked to completion.
items.risk: Agreed mitigations are never implemented.
items.test: For High residual risks, confirm a plan with owner and date, and evidence of completed actions.

categories.name: Policies, Procedures & Control Design
categories.objective: Expectations and controls are written down, current and designed to address the risks.

items.control: Policies are approved, published, version-controlled and reviewed at least annually.
items.risk: Staff follow outdated or unapproved rules.
items.test: Inspect policies for approval and review dates within 12 months.

items.control: Key processes have documented procedures or runbooks.
items.risk: Processes depend on individuals and fail when they are absent.
items.test: For sampled key processes, confirm a current procedure exists and matches practice through a walkthrough.

items.control: Policy exceptions are requested, risk-assessed, approved and time-bound.
items.risk: Exceptions become permanent, unmanaged deviations.
items.test: For sampled exceptions, confirm risk assessment, approval and an unexpired end date.

items.control: A risk-control matrix maps each risk to controls with owner, frequency, type and evidence, and identifies key controls.
items.risk: Risks lack controls, or controls exist without a clear purpose.
items.test: Inspect the RCM for completeness against the risk register and confirm key controls are identified.

items.control: Control design is assessed to confirm each key control would mitigate its risk if operated as intended.
items.risk: Controls are performed but do not actually address the risk.
items.test: Inspect design assessments for sampled key controls and confirm design gaps were remediated.

categories.name: Access Control
categories.objective: Access to systems and data in scope is approved, appropriate and promptly removed.

items.control: Access to in-scope systems and data is approved by the owner before it is granted, following least privilege.
items.risk: Users obtain unauthorised or excessive access.
items.test: For 25 sampled grants, confirm owner approval preceded access.

items.control: Owners recertify access periodically, and inappropriate access is removed.
items.risk: Inappropriate access accumulates.
items.test: Inspect review completeness, sign-off and completion of removals.

items.control: Leavers' access is removed within one business day and reconciled to HR records.
items.risk: Former staff retain access.
items.test: For 25 leavers, compare termination date to disable date.

items.control: Privileged access is restricted, protected by MFA and logged.
items.risk: Admin access is misused or compromised.
items.test: Inspect the privileged user list, MFA enforcement and activity logging.

items.control: A segregation-of-duties matrix is defined and conflicts are monitored and mitigated.
items.risk: One person can initiate and approve a transaction, enabling fraud or error.
items.test: Inspect the SoD matrix and conflict report, and confirm mitigations for accepted conflicts.

categories.name: Data Protection
categories.objective: Data in scope is classified, protected, retained appropriately and recoverable.

items.control: Data in scope is classified, and handling rules follow from the classification.
items.risk: Sensitive data is handled with too little protection.
items.test: Inspect the classification scheme and confirm sampled datasets are labelled correctly.

items.control: Confidential data is encrypted at rest and in transit.
items.risk: Data is exposed when storage or traffic is compromised.
items.test: Inspect encryption settings for sampled data stores and endpoints, and TLS configuration.

items.control: Personal data is processed only for documented purposes with a lawful basis.
items.risk: Privacy laws are breached.
items.test: Inspect the record of processing for in-scope processing and confirm DPIAs for high-risk processing.

items.control: Retention and disposal rules are applied, and records are securely destroyed at end of life.
items.risk: Data is kept too long, or destroyed too early.
items.test: Compare configured retention to the schedule, and inspect destruction records.

items.control: Data supporting critical processes is backed up, and restores are tested.
items.risk: Data cannot be recovered after loss or corruption.
items.test: Inspect backup job results and the latest restore test.
evidence: Backup scope compared to critical systems

categories.name: Change Management
categories.objective: Changes to processes, systems and controls are assessed, tested and approved.

items.control: Changes to in-scope systems are tested and approved by someone independent of the implementer before release.
items.risk: Unauthorised or defective changes disrupt operations.
items.test: For 25 sampled changes, confirm test evidence and independent approval before release.
evidence: Sampled tickets with tests and approvals

items.control: Changes to processes and systems are assessed for their impact on controls before implementation.
items.risk: Changes silently break or bypass controls.
items.test: For significant changes in the period, confirm a control impact assessment and RCM updates.

items.control: Emergency changes are approved retrospectively within a defined window.
items.risk: The emergency route is used to bypass control.
items.test: For emergency changes, confirm retrospective approval within the window.

items.control: Key spreadsheets and reports used in controls are inventoried, access-restricted and validated for completeness and accuracy after changes.
items.risk: Controls rely on reports or spreadsheets that are incomplete or wrong.
items.test: For sampled key reports, inspect completeness and accuracy validation and access restrictions.

categories.name: Third-Party Risk
categories.objective: Risks that third parties introduce are assessed, contracted and monitored.

items.control: Third parties supporting the area are inventoried and risk-tiered.
items.risk: High-risk suppliers are not identified for oversight.
items.test: Compare the inventory to accounts payable vendors and confirm tiering for a sample.

items.control: Due diligence proportionate to risk is completed before onboarding.
items.risk: Unsuitable suppliers are engaged.
items.test: For onboardings in the period, confirm due diligence approval before contract start.

items.control: Contracts include control requirements, audit rights, incident notification and exit clauses.
items.risk: The organisation cannot enforce expectations on suppliers.
items.test: Check sampled contracts against the clause checklist.

items.control: Supplier performance and risk are monitored, with critical suppliers reassessed annually.
items.risk: Supplier deterioration is noticed too late.
items.test: For critical suppliers, inspect SLA reports and the latest reassessment.

items.control: Exit plans exist for critical suppliers, and offboarding removes access and recovers data.
items.risk: The organisation is stranded or exposed when a supplier relationship ends.
items.test: Inspect exit plans for critical suppliers and offboarding records for terminated suppliers.
evidence: Access removal and data return confirmation

categories.name: Monitoring & Logging
categories.objective: Risk and control performance is measured, tested, logged and reported to decision-makers.

items.control: Key risk indicators have thresholds and escalation triggers and are reported monthly.
items.risk: Risk levels rise without anyone noticing.
items.test: Inspect KRI reports for three months and confirm breaches were escalated.

items.control: First-line control owners perform risk and control self-assessments (RCSA) and attest to control operation.
items.risk: Control failures are not surfaced by the people closest to them.
items.test: Inspect RCSA results and confirm self-identified issues were logged.

items.control: Key controls are independently tested for operating effectiveness by the second line or Internal Audit.
items.risk: Controls are assumed effective but are failing.
items.test: Inspect the test plan, sample sizes and results for key controls.

items.control: Control deficiencies are evaluated for severity and reported promptly to management and, where significant, to the board.
items.risk: Significant weaknesses are not escalated.
items.test: Inspect deficiency evaluations and the reporting to management and the board.

items.control: Activity on in-scope systems is logged, and significant events are reviewed.
items.risk: Misuse cannot be detected or reconstructed.
items.test: Inspect logging configuration and evidence of periodic review.

items.control: Risk reports summarising posture, issues and trends go to senior management on a set cadence.
items.risk: Leadership makes decisions without risk information.
items.test: Inspect reports for each quarter and their distribution.

categories.name: Incident & Issue Management
categories.objective: Incidents, losses and issues are captured, resolved at root cause, notified where required and learned from.

items.control: A defined process governs how incidents and loss events are reported, classified and escalated.
items.risk: Incidents are handled inconsistently or not escalated.
items.test: Inspect the procedure and, for sampled incidents, confirm classification and escalation per the procedure.

items.control: Loss events and near misses are captured in a central log and analysed for trends.
items.risk: Recurring loss patterns go unnoticed.
items.test: Inspect the loss event log and quarterly trend analysis.

items.control: Issues are managed through root cause analysis and action plans, and closure is independently validated.
items.risk: Issues are closed without being fixed.
items.test: For sampled closed issues, confirm RCA, completed actions and independent validation.

items.control: Regulatory and contractual notification obligations are assessed for each incident and met within deadlines.
items.risk: Missed notifications lead to penalties.
items.test: For incidents in the period, confirm a notification assessment and timely notifications where required.
evidence: Regulator and customer notifications with dates

items.control: Lessons learned from incidents and tests are fed back into risk assessments and controls.
items.risk: The same failures recur.
items.test: For major incidents, confirm a lessons-learned review and resulting control or risk updates.

categories.name: Business Continuity
categories.objective: Critical processes can continue or recover within acceptable timeframes during disruption.

items.control: A business impact analysis and continuity plans cover critical processes, with defined recovery objectives.
items.risk: Critical processes stop for longer than the business can tolerate.
items.test: Inspect the BIA and plans for critical processes, approval dates and recovery objectives.

items.control: Continuity and recovery plans are tested at least annually, and gaps are fixed.
items.risk: Plans fail when needed.
items.test: Inspect test reports and confirm gaps were remediated.

items.control: A crisis communication plan with pre-approved templates covers staff, customers, regulators and media.
items.risk: Poor communication during a crisis damages trust.
items.test: Inspect the plan, contact lists and templates for currency.
